Frank: I know you already took the programming course. Would you help me understand some things about JavaScript?
Camille: Sure! JavaScript is a dynamic programming language for browsers, servers, games, and even robot applications that directs the behavior of the different components of a website.
Frank: But why is it so important if there are more programming languages already?

Camille: Because it improves the user's experience. If most people weren't so visual, it wouldn't be as popular. Moreover, there are some important features you must take into account if you haven't used JavaScript before.
First, JavaScript is a lightweight program which means that it doesn't need much memory to run and it's easy to implement. Second, it allows client-side script that means it runs on the user's computer or browser. Third, it is object-oriented which focuses on objects presented in a web page, rather than the logic necessary for their manipulation. And fourth, it has network-centric characteristics which means that it interconnects people, services, information, and devices aiming to make the most out of resources.
Frank: Could we further discuss what Client-side JavaScript is?
Camille: Sure, this is the most common form of language. If JavaScript didn't allow client-side scripts, it wouldn't be as interactive as it permits the user to have more control over the program.

Frank: Wow, it sounds like a very complete application.
Camille: But it's not. It also has its limitations that need to be considered. For instance, reading or writing files is not allowed for security reasons. If you are planning to use JavaSript for networking applications, you won't be able to do so as it's not available, and it doesn't count with multiprocessor capabilities either.
Frank: True, but you can't deny the advantages that it has. Less server interaction lessens the load on user's server. Immediate feedback to visitors reduces time. And along with the increased interactivity, there is a richer interface.
Camille: You're right. Those are things we can't overlook.

Conditional Sentences With If Clauses: Negative Form
A conditional sentence states something that happens, will happen, could have happened, or could happen depending on a condition.

Conditional statements are called like this because they talk about situations that need a condition to be true or not. There are different types of conditional sentences that show the likelihood of a given result to take place or that speculate about what could have resulted from situations that didn't occur in the past or from unreal or imaginary events. Every type of conditional sentence has its own grammar structure.

The usual conditional sentence is composed of two clauses: the “if clause” that explains the condition, and the "main clause" that presents the result or consequence.

If you want to make a negative conditional statement, you can make either the “if clause” or the “result clause” negative, however, you have to pay attention to what you want to express. Let's take a look at some examples:

If you don't have money, you can't go.
If you don't have money, you can go.
If you have money, you can't go.

If you observe the examples carefully, you'll notice that the meaning of what is being uttered changes significantly with each sentence so, don't forget to bear in mind what you want to communicate when deciding which of the clauses is going to be negative.

Where is Javascript today?
There are different updates and versions for JavaScript.

There are some updates and versions that have gradually improved gradually JavaScript. However, it's been a long time since it was updated or improved. As a result, the latest update is the ECMAScript where JavaScript adapts itself to fulfill the ECMA International standards.

Even though changes are not notorious, it actually adds useful and more advanced features that have been requested by JavaScript users.
